newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh prison unrest eases, one jail holds out.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh prison unrest eases, one jail holds out.

text.p: A six-day revolt in Bangladeshi jails appeared to ease on Saturday after an uprising was crushed in Dhaka's central jail and a prison siege in northwestern Tangail ended peacefully, police and government officials said.
All but one of the revolts, triggered by the release of 90 prisoners under an amnesty marking the country's 25th independence anniversary on Monday, was over on Saturday.
Prisoners, angered at being excluded from the amnesty, were demanding freedom while others sought better treatment and food.
Prisoners in southwestern Jessore Jail, who began their revolt on Monday, were still refusing to give up on Saturday.

Officials said prisoners in Tangail ended their revolt late on Friday after a popular ruling party legislator pursuaded them to return to their cells. The jail inmates also set free five officials they had been holding hostage since Thursday.
On Friday, jail guards in Dhaka foiled an attempted revolt after fighting prisoners armed with knives and iron rods. At least 35 inmates and 15 guards were injured, police said.
Guards suppressed a third revolt in southern Barisal Jail on Thursday after about an hour of fighting.
Police said the prisoners in Jessore agreed to meet officials on Saturday to air their grievances.
"We are now hopeful of a peaceful ending to the crisis," said one police officer.
